site.name: MineForAll
site.description: A map of mining permits, satellite-mapped mining footprint, protected areas, and environmental impact, compiled from credible public data for transparency in Indonesia's mining industry.

about.title: About MineForAll
about.intro: MineForAll is an independent, non-profit observatory that distills credible satellite and public data on mining permits, satellite-mapped mining footprint, and their impacts on protected areas and communities in Indonesia into one open map anyone can check.
about.nameBody: 'Mine' refers to mining; 'ForAll' means for everyone. MineForAll means mining data transparency for all people — not just corporations or regulators, but for the broader public who have the right to know what is happening on their land.
about.whyBody: Indonesia's mining industry drives the economy, but its environmental and social impacts are often opaque. Many people do not know which mining permits operate in their area, or how close they are to protected zones. MineForAll assembles scattered data so anyone can see, understand, and act.
about.whatBody: We gather data from credible sources and show it as it is:
about.layer1: Annual tree cover loss (Hansen/UMD, 30 m resolution)
about.layer2: Palm, pulpwood, logging concessions, and the mining footprint
about.layer3: Protected & moratorium areas, National Parks, Wildlife Reserves, Nature Reserves, and more
about.p1Body: We gather and show scattered data, and let the reader judge for themselves. No accusations, no verdicts against anyone.
about.p2Body: Anything on the map traces back to its source dataset, with the retrieval date and license.
about.p3Body: The whole data pipeline and code are open source. Anyone can re-run it and get the same numbers.
about.p4Body: We don't sell data, run ads, or take sides.
about.openBody: Mine For All is AGPL-3.0 licensed and open to contributions from everyone. Each dataset remains the property of its source, see the Data Sources and Credits pages.

home.heroTitle: Where are the mines? You have the right to know.
home.heroBody: Thousands of mining permits are spread across Indonesia — coal, nickel, gold, copper. Some overlap with protected areas, some impact water sources and communities. We compile credible satellite and public data into one easy-to-understand map, so anyone can see what is happening on their land.
home.threadsBody: MineForAll was born from the belief that public data should be accessible to everyone, not just experts. Here is part of the story.
home.principle1Body: We show official data and satellite imagery side by side, so you can read and compare them yourself.
home.principle2Body: Anything on screen traces back to its source dataset in at most two clicks.
home.principle3Body: Our pipeline is open: anyone can re-run it and get the same numbers.
home.mission1Body: These forests are the last home of the Sumatran elephant, the tiger, and the orangutan. Every hectare lost pushes them out and conflict with humans almost always ends badly for them.
home.mission2Body: Bare hills upstream mean floods and landslides downstream. We link disaster records to forest loss within the same watershed, so the connection is plain to see.
home.mission3Title: For those who work the land
home.mission3Body: Many people depend on this land for a living, and we are not here to judge. We show the data as it is, so everyone understands the consequences of what happens on the ground.
home.ctaBody: Awareness begins with clear information. Open the map, explore your region, and share what you find.
home.nameMine: 'mine', the central focus of our transparency and monitoring
home.nameForAll: 'for all', open data accessible to everyone without restriction or monopoly
home.nameMeaning: Mine For All means mining data transparency for everyone — not corporate secrets or bureaucratic hurdles, but open public information so citizens can understand what is happening to the land.
home.publicInterest: Mine For All is an independent, non-profit public-interest observatory. We don't sell data, run ads, or take sides. We assemble credible satellite and public data into one open map anyone can check, all of the code is open source, and every record traces back to its source.
home.campaignCaption: Get to know who lives near you. Threatened wildlife may be closer than you think.
home.storyBody: A cinematic flight over Tesso Nilo: what remains, what's been lost, and who still lives there. Data and sources, woven into one story.
home.storyLeuserBody: Climb the spine of the Barisan Range, where four of Sumatra’s giants still share one forest. Mountains, mist, and the wildlife that remains, in a single journey.
home.giantsBody: In the same forest, Sumatra's great animals still hold on. Every hectare lost narrows the space they have left.
home.showcaseTitle: Every layer, on a single map
home.showcaseBody: Deforestation, concessions, protected areas, and wildlife sightings, woven into one map you can rotate, tilt, and explore down to the village.
home.showcase3dBody: See forests and mountains in real relief. Tilt the earth, fly over the landscape, and feel the scale.
home.showcaseFlatBody: Compare concessions and protected areas side by side across the archipelago, from Sumatra to Papua.
home.ktpCtaSub: Make your forest ID and share it
home.supportCtaSub: Follow the journey and lend support

campaign.title: Who Lives Near You
campaign.intro: Protected wildlife often feels far away, in the forest, out at sea, in the news, in the numbers. Yet some of it might live not far from your home. We can't love what we don't know, so let's get to know the wildlife living near you first. Then introduce it to the people closest to you.

wetlandInfo.mangrove: Mangrove forest: a coastal vegetation belt that buffers erosion and storms, stores 'blue' carbon many times that of inland forest, and is a fish nursery and home for proboscis monkeys, crocodiles, and water birds. 2020 extent from satellite imagery (Global Mangrove Watch v3).
wetlandInfo.peatland: Peatland: carbon-rich wetland soil built up over millennia. Drained and burned it releases enormous carbon and drives the haze; kept wet it is vital habitat for orangutans, tigers, and swamp wildlife.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: Every layer in Mine For All has a source, a retrieval date, and a methodology. This page explains where the data comes from, how it is processed, and its limitations.
methodology.limitsBody: Satellite tree-cover-loss detection has false positives and is not always deforestation; pixel resolution is 10-30 m; public concession boundaries can be outdated. The methodology version is stamped on every derived record and every change is noted in this changelog.
methodology.disclaimerBody: Mine For All assembles public third-party data and presents it as-is; it draws no conclusions, accuses no one, and does not assert that any party has broken the law. Names of companies, concessions, and places come from the source datasets, not from us. Overlaps between layers are context, not verdicts, and tree cover loss is not always illegal deforestation. We honour the presumption of innocence, and we welcome correction requests, which we review and fix.

sources.title: Data Sources
sources.intro: Every dataset shown on the map is listed here so you can verify it yourself: source organization, link, license, last update, coverage, and description. We never fabricate coordinates, habitat ranges, mining locations, or conservation data.
sources.gapsIntro: We could not find credible open data for the following. We name the provider it should come from rather than guess.
sources.disclaimerBody: Everything here is gathered from credible third-party public sources and shown as-is, unaltered. Company, concession, and location names come directly from the source datasets, not from us, and are not accusations. Mine For All draws no legal conclusions and accuses no one: an overlap between layers (for example, tree cover loss inside a concession) is not a claim that any law was broken, and tree cover loss is not always illegal deforestation. We respect the presumption of innocence. If any party believes a data point is inaccurate, please contact us and we will review and correct it.

project.title: The project
project.intro: Mine For All is built in the open, as a non-profit, public-interest project. This page explains where its source code stands and how you can get involved.
project.sourceBody: All of Mine For All's code is open-source (AGPL-3.0). The intent is simple: anyone can inspect how it works, copy it, and help improve it.
project.sourceStatus: The repository is currently being prepared for public release, together with contribution guidelines so anyone can take part comfortably. The repository link will appear here once it's ready.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer & Terms
disclaimer.updated: Applies to your use of mineforall.org.
disclaimer.intro: Mine For All is an independent, non-profit, public-interest observatory made for education and awareness. It compiles credible third-party public data about Indonesia's forests and shows it as-is. Please read the following before relying on anything here.
disclaimer.s1Body: This is a public-interest and educational project, not a legal, commercial, or investigative-journalism service. We publish data so the public can see and understand it. We do not sell it, run ads, or take sides.
disclaimer.s2Body: Every layer comes from a credible public source, cited on the Data Sources and Methodology pages, and is shown without alteration. Third-party data can be incomplete, out of date, or contain errors. It is provided on an 'as is' basis, with no warranty of accuracy or fitness for any purpose.
disclaimer.s3Title: Not an accusation, presumption of innocence
disclaimer.s3Body: Mine For All draws no conclusions and makes no allegations against any person or company. Names of companies, concessions, and places come directly from the source datasets, not from us. An overlap between layers (for example, tree cover loss inside a concession) is context, not a verdict, and tree cover loss is not always illegal deforestation. Nothing here is a determination that any party has broken the law; we uphold the presumption of innocence.
disclaimer.s4Body: If you are an affected party, or you spot data you believe is inaccurate, misleading, or objectionable, please tell us. Send a message via Threads DM and we will review it in good faith and correct, annotate, or remove the item promptly. The right of reply is always open.
disclaimer.s5Body: Use this site at your own discretion. Mine For All and its contributors are not liable for any loss or decision made in reliance on the information shown. For legal, commercial, or field decisions, verify against the original sources.
disclaimer.s6Body: The code is open source under AGPL-3.0. Each dataset remains the property of its source and is used under that source's licence; see the Data Sources and Credits pages.
disclaimer.s7Body: These terms may be updated as the project evolves. Continued use means you accept the current version.
disclaimer.contactNote: Corrections and right-of-reply requests are welcome and reviewed in good faith.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.updated: How Mine For All handles your data.
privacy.intro: Mine For All is built to need as little of your data as possible. There are no accounts, and we don't sell data. Here is exactly what happens.
privacy.s1Body: The 'Who lives near you' feature uses your location only inside your browser, to calculate distance, and never sends or stores it. Any photo you add for a Forest Resident Card is processed entirely on your device and is never uploaded. You can skip both.
privacy.s2Body: Anonymous, aggregate usage analytics (Google Analytics and Vercel Web Analytics) to understand which pages are useful, and a small functional cookie that remembers your light/dark theme. We do not build a personal profile of you.
privacy.s3Body: Pages load map tiles and assets from providers such as CARTO, Esri, Global Forest Watch, and public font/CDN hosts. As with any website, these may see your IP address as part of serving the request. Analytics is provided by Google and Vercel.
privacy.s4Body: We use a functional cookie only to remember your theme choice. Analytics may set its own cookies or identifiers; you can block these with your browser or an ad-blocker without breaking the site.
privacy.s5Body: Because we don't hold a personal profile of you, there is little to access or delete. If you have a privacy question or request, message us via Threads DM.
privacy.s6Body: We will update this page if our data practices change.
privacy.contactNote: Privacy questions and requests are welcome.

gate.title: Before you explore
gate.body: Mine For All visualises public datasets from various organisations, for education and data exploration. We make no accusations, findings of fact, or legal conclusions about any individual, company, or institution.
gate.body2: Names, boundaries, and attributes come from their respective source datasets. An overlap between layers is visual context to aid analysis, not evidence or a conclusion. We uphold the presumption of innocence.
